scope: A reviewed starting map for Marketing PhD job seekers across Quant / Modeling, Consumer Behavior and Strategy, with separate Economics / IO complements. Not an exhaustive directory or market census.

resources.title: AMA DocSIG · Who Went Where
resources.use: Annual survey archive for the experience of entering the academic market.
resources.limit: Self-selected responses. The 2025 geographic restriction and redesigned questions limit comparisons across editions.
resources.takeaway: Store survey edition, population and question-level sample sizes separately from person records.

resources.title: Who Went Where · 2025 full report
resources.region: North American PhD origin and/or hiring institution
resources.use: Read the tables behind the survey benchmarks below.
resources.limit: Anonymous survey responses cannot be linked to the separately volunteered placement names.
resources.takeaway: Never attach an aggregate salary, publication count or offer count to a named candidate.

resources.title: AMA · ELMAR job archive
resources.edition: Dated job announcements and searchable archive
resources.use: A central Marketing academic discovery channel, including Quant, CB, Strategy and mixed calls.
resources.limit: Announcement date is not the application deadline. One notice may link several positions, and duplicate notices may describe the same search.
resources.takeaway: Follow employer links and preserve original posting IDs; keep notices, positions and hires separate.

resources.title: AMA Academic Job Board
resources.edition: Live service; automated read returned HTTP 403
resources.use: Academic vacancy discovery across Marketing specializations; linked from the AMA website.
resources.limit: Listings were not fully readable in this review. Access failure says nothing about the number of available jobs.
resources.takeaway: Open the original advertisement and institution application page before recording a position.

resources.title: Academy of Marketing Science · Job Board
resources.use: A working academic job board and the current destination of a well-known historical Marketing aggregator.
resources.limit: The redirect does not establish that the former site's candidate profiles, archives or statistics survive.
resources.takeaway: Treat the two addresses as one discovery channel, not independent vacancy counts.

resources.title: Econ Job Market · Advertisements
resources.use: Search Marketing, Industrial Organization and relevant Business Economics calls; especially useful for the Quant / IO interface.
resources.limit: Some ads require login. An economics field label alone does not make a vacancy a Marketing position.
resources.takeaway: Separate full-consideration dates, application deadlines and posting end dates. Deduplicate by posting ID and institution.

resources.title: AEA · JOE Listings
resources.use: Find academic and nonacademic economics opportunities using JEL L and relevant M categories, then inspect research fit.
resources.limit: Adjacent-market discovery; this is not a Marketing census. Consult source terms before reuse or bulk collection.
resources.takeaway: Retain the actual department, rank and appointment type; do not relabel every IO job as Quant Marketing.

resources.title: AEA · EconTrack
resources.use: A model for following recruitment milestones and distinguishing institution-certified updates from other contributions.
resources.limit: Employer participation is voluntary. Unreported activity is not evidence that interviews or offers have not happened.
resources.takeaway: Track a search's status and its reporter, without exposing candidate-level interview or offer rumors.

resources.title: AEA · JOE Openings by Week
resources.edition: Landing page read; embedded charts not extracted
resources.use: Official economics demand-monitoring reference and a design model for comparing the same week across years.
resources.limit: No numerical chart values were imported. Economics trends should not be presented as Marketing trends.
resources.takeaway: Compare consistent calendar cutoffs and retain the underlying posting population.

resources.title: AEA · 2026 job market guidance
resources.use: Economics-cycle guidance for candidates also applying through the economics market.
resources.limit: Recommendations are market-specific; individual employers may use different dates.
resources.takeaway: Maintain a separate Economics / IO calendar alongside the Marketing calendar.

resources.title: AMA · Academic job market guidelines
resources.edition: 2022 guidance, retained as a dated reference
resources.use: Understand the association's recommended interview, flyout and offer sequence.
resources.limit: A historical recommendation is not an enforced 2026 timetable. Source publication year must remain visible.
resources.takeaway: Use current employer deadlines for applications and label recommendations separately from observed behavior.

resources.title: Ron Berman · Marketing market analysis
resources.use: A directly relevant faculty-authored analysis of Marketing hiring activity and timing.
resources.limit: An individual's analysis, not an official market census. Posting schools, advertisements and actual positions are different units.
resources.takeaway: Borrow the dated comparisons and separate units; do not treat the author's forecast as an observed annual result.

resources.title: Econ PhD Placements
resources.use: A close product reference: cohort coverage, searchable first jobs, department comparisons, employer profiles and CSV downloads.
resources.limit: Its methodology can classify an employer-only university placement as tenure-track and warns of upward bias.
resources.takeaway: Borrow coverage and employer views. Preserve this project's stronger rule: missing titles or contracts keep tenure unknown.

resources.title: EMAC · Job Market
resources.edition: Visible listings explicitly marked DEMO / fictional
resources.use: Reference for filtering by marketing area, region, rank and contract type.
resources.limit: The three visible examples at review were fictional. They are excluded from this project's job data.
resources.takeaway: Recheck for real advertisements before using this page as a vacancy feed.

resources.title: EMAC · Job Market Training
resources.use: Application feedback and practice interviews with separate Quant and CB tracks.
resources.limit: Training participation is not a placement observation or guarantee; check the live call for conditions.
resources.takeaway: Offer a preparation-resource layer alongside market records.

resources.title: ACR · Community E-List
resources.use: A consumer-research announcement channel that includes job openings.
resources.limit: A mailing list is a discovery channel, not a structured public archive of all CB jobs.
resources.takeaway: Resolve an announcement to the institution's original vacancy before adding it.

resources.title: Society for Consumer Psychology · Jobs
resources.edition: Extracted page showed a job-widget placeholder
resources.use: An additional CB discovery entry point.
resources.limit: No individual live listing was verified in this review; do not interpret the empty extraction as zero openings.
resources.takeaway: Retain access limitations and verify each employer link separately.

resources.title: AMA · PhD Programs in Marketing
resources.use: A starting list for extending the sending-program frame beyond North America, Hong Kong and Singapore.
resources.limit: Includes DBA institutions and does not verify active PhD cohorts or research tracks. Research rankings are a separate concept.
resources.takeaway: Verify program eligibility, then locate candidate and placement pages for each program-year.

resources.title: Wharton · Marketing placements
resources.use: Named graduates and initial destinations, including nonacademic employers.
resources.limit: The year is degree year; a first-job start year requires separate evidence. Public rows alone do not prove cohort completeness.
resources.takeaway: Keep graduation year, job start year and source-table year distinct.

resources.title: Columbia · Marketing PhD
resources.use: Official destinations with examples of postdocs and sequential industry / academic arrangements.
resources.limit: A general PhD-student profile is not proof of current market participation; distinguish student and job-market sections.
resources.takeaway: Represent multiple appointments as dated events, without replacing the initial job.

resources.title: HBS · Marketing doctoral placement
resources.use: A useful source format linking initial destination, dissertation and advisors.
resources.limit: A dissertation title is not automatically a job market paper; named successful placements do not establish all graduates.
resources.takeaway: Save dissertation and JMP as separate material types.

resources.title: Purdue · Marketing job market candidates
resources.use: Department candidate roster with research titles, committees and CV links.
resources.limit: Expected graduation is not a completed PhD. Determine research track from explicit candidate evidence.
resources.takeaway: Retain expected dates and confirmed dates separately; snapshot rosters before they change.

resources.title: Kellogg · Doctoral job placements
resources.use: A school-level placement source with Marketing among other doctoral programs.
resources.limit: Other Kellogg fields, including Managerial Economics and Strategy, must not be automatically counted as Marketing.
resources.takeaway: Use the actual doctoral program and explicit research labels.

resources.title: MIT Sloan · Recent academic placements
resources.edition: Page describes where graduates are today
resources.use: Graduate identities, degree years and observed academic affiliations.
resources.limit: Despite its title, this page describes current destinations, not necessarily first placements. It omits nonacademic paths by design.
resources.takeaway: Confirm first jobs independently from CVs or contemporaneous announcements.

resources.title: Stanford GSB · Academic placements
resources.edition: Existing project source; HTTP 403 on this review
resources.use: A priority follow-up source in the existing Quant / Marketing program frame.
resources.limit: No fresh person-level facts were confirmed from this URL in this review.
resources.takeaway: Keep existing evidence dates; do not turn an access attempt into factual re-verification.

resources.title: NYU Stern · Marketing PhD placements
resources.edition: Existing project source; HTTP 403 on this review
resources.use: A priority follow-up source in the existing Quant / Marketing program frame.
resources.limit: No fresh person-level facts were confirmed from this URL in this review.
resources.takeaway: Try department-linked candidate pages and individual CVs, preserving access-failure history.

resources.title: NUS · Marketing student placements
resources.use: An Asia-based sending-program source for the existing project scope.
resources.limit: Page accessibility does not establish that the latest cohort has been published or completely recorded.
resources.takeaway: Audit each source year, then inspect individual research fields and destination dates.

resources.title: INSEAD · PhD community and placements
resources.edition: 2026/27 candidate entry point and alumni placement section
resources.use: A priority addition to the sending-program frame across Europe and Asia.
resources.limit: The school-wide page spans multiple disciplines. A headline or overall placement statement is not a Marketing cohort denominator.
resources.takeaway: Follow named Marketing candidates and distinguish campus, degree program and destination.

resources.title: Tilburg · Marketing PhD and placements
resources.edition: Explicit Modeling / CB / Strategy program description
resources.use: A three-track program reference with both academic and professional placement examples.
resources.limit: Listed examples are historical and some do not name individuals; they are not a full current cohort.
resources.takeaway: Preserve unnamed aggregate evidence without inventing people or inferring track from employer.

resources.title: Tilburg · 2026–2027 job market candidates
resources.use: An example of a dated school-wide roster with fields, JMPs and placement officers.
resources.limit: Check the current discipline sections; absence of a Marketing section does not prove zero Marketing candidates.
resources.takeaway: Track roster publication and field-specific completeness separately.

resources.title: London Business School · Placement archive
resources.use: A European expansion reference with named graduates, subject codes and job titles.
resources.limit: Historical coverage only; a Marketing-related employer or title does not make a graduate with another subject code a Marketing PhD.
resources.takeaway: Use the MKT program code, and find newer official cohorts before making current comparisons.

survey.population: North American doctoral origin and/or North American appointment; self-reported survey.
survey.caution: Question sample sizes vary. These all-track respondent averages are neither Quant-specific targets nor market-wide success rates.
